sources.entry: HTMLy - Databaseless PHP blogging platform. A flat-file CMS that allows you to create a fast, secure, and powerful website or blog in seconds. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: HTMLy is a databaseless, flat-file PHP blogging platform focused on simplicity and speed.
summary.what_it_does: HTMLy is a blogging platform written in PHP that stores content in flat files rather than a database. According to the README, it finds and lists content by date, type, category, tag, or author using a custom algorithm. The README claims performance stays fast with ten thousand posts and hundreds of tags. It includes a browser-based installer and an online installer option. An admin dashboard is available at /login, and admin-role users can edit or delete all users' posts. Themes are referenced as a separate resource.
use_cases: run a personal blog without a database
publish a simple website or blog quickly
list posts by tag, category, or author
manage multi-author blog posts with an admin role
how_to_run: Download the latest version from the GitHub repo
Upload and extract the zip file to your web server (root directory or a subdirectory such as htmly)
Visit your domain and follow the installer
Delete install.php manually if it still exists after installation
Set write permission for the cache and content directories
Access the admin panel by adding /login to the site URL
notable: Databaseless flat-file design with no database setup
Content listing by date, type, category, tag, or author
Online installer option that avoids downloading the full source
Simple manual activation: rename config.ini.example to config.ini to skip dashboard login
caveats: Requires PHP 7.2 or greater with several PHP extensions; the ZIP extension is needed for the backup feature
Installer and online-installer.php must be deleted manually if they remain after setup
Write permissions are required on the cache and content directories
keywords: run a blog on shared hosting
